flows.name: Visit landing page
flows.goal: Understand what StudioDesk is for and get started.
flows.outcome: Nothing is stored; the visitor reaches sign-up, sign-in, or the public booking page.
flows.description: A visitor arrives on the public StudioDesk landing page which explains it is one calm workspace for a solo freelance designer to run clients, projects, and bookings, then chooses to sign up or sign in as the designer or to open the public booking page as a booker.

flows.name: Designer signs up
flows.goal: Create an account and reach the home screen.
flows.outcome: A new designer account exists and sign-in persists; after refresh she is still signed in on the home screen.
flows.description: A new designer enters an email and password on the sign-up screen, submits, and lands directly on her home screen with an empty workspace ready for her first client, seeing only her own data afterwards.

flows.name: Designer signs in
flows.goal: Sign back in to the workspace.
flows.outcome: The designer is signed in and stays signed in after a refresh.
flows.description: A returning designer enters her email and password on the sign-in screen, submits, and returns to her home screen with today's sessions, follow-ups due this week, and overdue tasks.

flows.name: Designer signs out
flows.goal: Leave the workspace securely.
flows.outcome: The designer is signed out; a refresh still shows the signed-out landing page.
flows.description: The signed-in designer chooses to sign out from anywhere in the app and is returned to the public landing page, with her data kept for the next sign-in.

flows.name: Add a client
flows.goal: Remember a new client for the first time.
flows.outcome: The new client is saved and still appears in the client list after a refresh.
flows.description: The designer adds a client with name, email, optional company, profile, status, and optional follow-up date, saves it, and sees it appear in the client list where it persists.

flows.name: View clients and handle follow-ups
flows.goal: See who needs a follow-up and act in one click.
flows.outcome: Follow-up dates updated by done or push-a-week persist and the sorted order still shows after a refresh.
flows.description: The designer opens the client list sorted with overdue follow-ups first, then soonest, then no date, sees who is due, and with one click marks a follow-up done which clears its date or pushes it a week which adds seven days.

flows.name: Edit a client
flows.goal: Keep a client's details and follow-up date up to date.
flows.outcome: Client changes are saved and still show after a refresh.
flows.description: The designer opens a client, changes its name, email, company, profile, status, or follow-up date, saves, and sees the updated client details and list position.

flows.name: Delete a client
flows.goal: Remove a client and everything under it.
flows.outcome: The client, its projects, tasks, and notes are gone and stay gone after a refresh.
flows.description: The designer chooses to delete a client, confirms, and sees it removed together with its projects, their tasks, and its notes, while sessions themselves remain with that client's seats freed.

flows.name: Add and view client notes
flows.goal: Keep call history and next follow-up under the client.
flows.outcome: New notes and the follow-up date are saved under the client and still show after a refresh.
flows.description: The designer opens a client, views its dated notes newest first, jots a new note with date and text, sets or changes the follow-up date, and can delete a mistaken note.

flows.name: Add a project
flows.goal: Start tracking a piece of work for a client.
flows.outcome: The new project is saved under its client and still appears with zero open tasks after a refresh.
flows.description: The designer creates a project under a chosen client with a name, short description, and optional due date, saves it, and sees it in the project list with its open task count.

flows.name: Edit a project
flows.goal: Keep a project's details correct.
flows.outcome: Project changes are saved and still show after a refresh.
flows.description: The designer opens a project, edits its name, description, or due date, saves, and sees the updated project in the list and detail view.

flows.name: Delete a project
flows.goal: Remove a project and its tasks.
flows.outcome: The project and its tasks are gone and stay gone after a refresh.
flows.description: The designer chooses to delete a project, confirms, and sees it removed together with all its tasks while the parent client remains.

flows.name: View project list with open counts
flows.goal: See all projects and how much work is still open on each.
flows.outcome: Nothing is changed; the same projects with their current open task counts still show after a refresh.
flows.description: The designer opens the project list and sees every project with how many of its tasks are still open, then opens a project to continue work on it.

flows.name: View and find tasks in a project
flows.goal: Find the right tasks inside a project.
flows.outcome: Nothing is changed; the same filtered task list still shows after a refresh.
flows.description: The designer opens a project to see its tasks with overdue tasks standing out, searches by title and filters by status and priority to find the tasks she needs, then opens a task to continue work on it.

flows.name: Add a task
flows.goal: Add a new task to a project.
flows.outcome: The new task is saved in its project and still appears after a refresh.
flows.description: The designer opens a project, adds a new task with title, status, priority, and optional due date, saves it, and sees it appear in the task list with updated open counts.

flows.name: Edit a task
flows.goal: Keep a task up to date and tick it Done.
flows.outcome: Task changes including Done status are saved and still show after a refresh.
flows.description: The designer opens a task, changes its title, status, priority, or due date including ticking it Done quickly or moving it back to To do or In progress, saves, and sees the updated task and open counts.

flows.name: Delete a task
flows.goal: Remove a task that is no longer needed.
flows.outcome: The task is gone and stays gone after a refresh.
flows.description: The designer chooses to delete a task from its project, confirms, and sees it removed with updated open counts while the project remains.

flows.name: Set weekly availability
flows.goal: Publish when bookers can book her.
flows.outcome: Weekly availability is saved and still shows after a refresh.
flows.description: The designer sets her weekly availability by choosing which days and from what time to what time she can be booked, saves it, and sees it used to generate open slots for the next two weeks.

flows.name: Add a session type
flows.goal: Offer a new kind of bookable session.
flows.outcome: The new session type is saved and still shows on the booking page after a refresh.
flows.description: The designer adds a new session type with name, duration, displayed price, and maximum people, saves it, and sees it offered on the public booking page.

flows.name: Edit a session type
flows.goal: Keep a session type's details correct.
preconditions: At least one session type exists.
flows.outcome: Session type changes are saved and still show on the booking page after a refresh.
flows.description: The designer opens a session type from the default discovery call, design review, and Figma workshop types or one she added, edits its name, duration, price display, or maximum people, saves, and sees the updated type on the booking page.

flows.name: Delete a session type
flows.goal: Stop offering a session type.
preconditions: At least one session type exists.
flows.outcome: The session type is gone and stays gone after a refresh.
flows.description: The designer chooses to delete a session type she no longer offers, confirms, and sees it removed so bookers can no longer pick it, while existing sessions already booked for it remain.

flows.name: Book a session from public page
flows.goal: Book a session without creating an account.
preconditions: Designer has set availability and at least one session type.
flows.outcome: The booking is saved on its session and under the matched or newly created Lead client, and the slot shows one fewer free seat after a refresh.
flows.description: A booker without an account opens the public booking page, picks a session type with its displayed price, sees open slots for the next two weeks with full slots marked full, picks a slot, books with name and email, and sees a confirmation with a cancellation link on screen; a matching client email links the booking to that client, otherwise a new Lead client is created.

flows.name: Cancel a booking via link
flows.goal: Cancel my own booking.
preconditions: Booker has a valid cancellation link from a booking.
flows.outcome: The booking is cancelled and stays cancelled after a refresh, with its seat available again.
flows.description: A booker opens the unique cancellation link shown after booking, views the booking details, and cancels just their own booking, freeing the seat for others.

flows.name: View upcoming sessions and cancel a slot
flows.goal: Run upcoming sessions and cancel a slot when needed.
flows.outcome: Cancelled sessions and their bookings stay cancelled after a refresh.
flows.description: The designer opens upcoming sessions with seats booked versus maximum, sees who booked each slot, and cancels a whole slot which cancels everyone booked on it.

flows.name: View home dashboard
flows.goal: Start the day knowing what needs attention.
flows.outcome: Nothing is changed; the same today's sessions, due follow-ups, and overdue tasks still show after a refresh.
flows.description: The designer opens her home screen to see today's sessions, follow-ups due this week including overdue styling, and overdue tasks, and jumps to the relevant client, project, or session from each item.

fields.label: Designer email
fields.meaning: Email the designer uses to sign up and sign in

fields.label: Password
fields.meaning: Secret that proves the designer owns the account

fields.label: Client name
fields.meaning: How the designer refers to the client

fields.label: Client email
fields.meaning: Email used to contact the client and to match bookings

fields.label: Company
fields.meaning: Client company, when the client has one

fields.label: Profile
fields.meaning: Short profile of what the client does, how they met, and what they pay
fields.example: Runs a D2C store, met at a design meetup, pays per project

fields.label: Client status
fields.meaning: Whether the client is a Lead, Active, or Past

fields.label: Follow-up date

fields.label: Note date

fields.label: Note text

fields.example: Discussed homepage rework, will share wireframes next week

fields.label: Project name
fields.meaning: How the designer refers to the piece of work

fields.label: Project description
fields.meaning: Short summary of what the project covers

fields.label: Project due date
fields.meaning: When the project should be finished, if there is a deadline

fields.label: Task title
fields.meaning: What needs to be done in the project

fields.label: Task status
fields.meaning: Whether the task is To do, In progress, or Done

fields.label: Task priority
fields.meaning: How urgent the task is: Low, Medium, or High

fields.label: Task due date
fields.meaning: When the task should be finished, if there is a deadline

fields.label: Available days
fields.meaning: Which weekdays the designer can be booked

fields.label: Available from
fields.meaning: Start of the bookable window on each available day

fields.label: Available to
fields.meaning: End of the bookable window on each available day

fields.label: Session type name
fields.meaning: How the bookable session is presented to bookers

fields.label: Duration in minutes
fields.meaning: How long one session lasts

fields.label: Price display
fields.meaning: Price shown for information only, or Free; nobody pays in the app

fields.label: Maximum people
fields.meaning: How many bookings a slot accepts before it is full

fields.label: Booker name
fields.meaning: Name of the person booking a session

fields.label: Booker email
fields.meaning: Email of the person booking, used to link to a client

fields.label: Search tasks
fields.meaning: Free text to find tasks by title inside a project

fields.label: Chosen session type
fields.meaning: Which kind of session the booker wants to book

fields.label: Chosen slot
fields.meaning: The specific date and start time the booker picks

steps.websiteResponse: The website asks to confirm the deletion and says what else will be removed with it.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website deletes the record and what belongs to it.
Nothing is deleted; the record stays as it was.

assumptions.text: Notes are append-only history: the designer can add and view notes and delete a mistaken note, but cannot edit a note's date or text after saving, to keep call history trustworthy.

The project list is sorted by project due date soonest first, with projects without a due date last, then by name. Inside a project, overdue tasks are highlighted and task filters default to showing all statuses and priorities.

Until the designer sets weekly availability, the public booking page shows no open slots and explains that no times are available yet. Availability changes apply to future slot generation only and never move or cancel existing Sessions or Bookings.
